These pages will provide deeper technical understanding of the components introduced here, enabling you to customize simulations for your specific research needs.

# System Object and Data Structures



The System object serves as Molly.jl's central state container, aggregating all components required for molecular dynamics simulations into a single cohesive structure. This architectural design ensures that simulation state, physical properties, and computational settings remain synchronized throughout the simulation lifecycle. The System type implements the AtomsBase.jl `AbstractSystem` interface, providing compatibility with the broader Julia ecosystem while maintaining Molly.jl-specific optimizations for performance-critical operations.

## System Architecture Overview

The System struct follows a parameterized design that statically encodes dimensional information and type parameters for performance optimization. All computational-critical data types are captured as type parameters, enabling compiler optimizations and eliminating runtime type checks. The architecture distinguishes between **dynamic state** (coordinates, velocities) that evolve during simulation and **static topology** (atoms, interactions, boundaries) that typically remains constant throughout simulation, except in specific scenarios like free energy calculations or replica exchange.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph System["System"]
        subgraph AtomicData["Atomic State"]
            A[atoms<br/>Bits type array]
            C[coords<br/>SVector array]
            V[velocities<br/>SVector array]
        end
        
        subgraph Topology["Molecular Topology"]
            AD[atoms_data<br/>String metadata]
            MT[topology<br/>MolecularTopology]
        end
        
        subgraph Interactions["Force Field"]
            PI[pairwise_inters<br/>LJ, Coulomb]
            SI[specific_inter_lists<br/>Bonds, Angles, Torsions]
            GI[general_inters<br/>Implicit solvent]
            CN[constraints<br/>SHAKE]
        end
        
        subgraph Simulation["Simulation Control"]
            B[boundary<br/>Cubic/Rectangular/Triclinic]
            NF[neighbor_finder<br/>Cell lists]
            LG[loggers<br/>Data collection]
        end
        
        subgraph Physics["Physical Constants"]
            FU[force_units]
            EU[energy_units]
            KC[k<br/>Boltzmann constant]
            DF[df<br/>Degrees of freedom]
            MS[masses<br/>Array]
            TM[total_mass]
        end
        
        subgraph Metadata["Metadata"]
            DA[data<br/>Arbitrary user data]
        end
    end
    
    AtomicData -->|force calculation| Interactions
    Topology -->|interaction lookup| Interactions
    Boundary -->|periodic images| AtomicData
    Simulation -->|coordinate updates| AtomicData
    Physics -->|energy conversion| Interactions
    Loggers -->|property recording| AtomicData
```

## Core System Fields

The System struct contains 21 fields organized into logical groups that map to simulation requirements. Understanding these fields is essential for both using and extending Molly.jl effectively.

**Atomic State Fields**: The `atoms` field holds an array of Atom instances, which are carefully designed as bits types for GPU compatibility. Each Atom encapsulates its physical properties: `index`, `atom_type`, `mass`, `charge`, `σ` (Lennard-Jones size parameter), and `ϵ` (Lennard-Jones energy parameter). The `coords` and `velocities` fields store the dynamic state as arrays of static vectors (typically `SVector{3}`), with velocities defaulting to zero-initialized values if not explicitly provided.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L200-L270), [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L420-L440)

**Boundary Conditions**: The `boundary` field defines the simulation domain using one of three concrete boundary types: `CubicBoundary`, `RectangularBoundary`, or `TriclinicBoundary`. Each boundary type implements the `AbstractBoundary{D, T, C}` interface parameterized by dimension, float type, and coordinate type, enabling compile-time optimization of boundary condition calculations including coordinate wrapping and minimum image convention.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L425-L440), [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L10-L80)

> [!TIP]
> The System constructor performs extensive validation to ensure GPU arrays and CPU arrays are consistently used across all fields. If atoms are GPU arrays, coordinates and velocities must also be GPU arrays, preventing expensive data transfers during simulation loops.

## Atom and AtomData Separation

Molly.jl employs a **two-tier architecture** for atom information to balance computational efficiency with metadata richness. The Atom struct stores only numeric, bits-type fields essential for force calculations, while AtomData contains string-based metadata required for analysis but not simulation dynamics.

### Atom Structure

The Atom struct uses Julia's `@kwdef` macro for convenient construction with keyword arguments:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `index` | `Int` | Atom index in the system array |
| `atom_type` | `T` | Integer type identifier for force field lookups |
| `mass` | `M` | Atomic mass (default: `1.0u"g/mol"`) |
| `charge` | `C` | Partial charge for electrostatics |
| `σ` | `S` | Lennard-Jones finite distance (default: `0.0u"nm"`) |
| `ϵ` | `E` | Lennard-Jones well depth (default: `0.0u"kJ * mol^-1"`) |

The type parameters `T, M, C, S, E` allow flexible field types while maintaining compile-time type stability for GPU execution.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L220-L250)

### AtomData Structure

AtomData stores non-numeric information that would prevent GPU compatibility if embedded in Atom:

```julia
@kwdef struct AtomData
    atom_type::String = "?"
    atom_name::String = "?"
    res_number::Int = 1
    res_name::String = "???"
    chain_id::String = "A"
    element::String = "?"
    hetero_atom::Bool = false
end
```

This separation enables efficient force calculation kernels that operate on arrays of bits-type Atoms while preserving rich metadata for trajectory analysis, structure output, and post-processing.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L330-L345)

## Interaction Organization

Molly.jl categorizes interactions into three distinct groups based on computational characteristics, each with optimized data structures for efficient evaluation.

### Pairwise Interactions

The `pairwise_inters` field contains a tuple or named tuple of `PairwiseInteraction` subtypes, which are actually aliases for `NBodyInteraction{2}`. These interactions operate on most atom pairs and typically require neighbor lists for efficient computation. Common examples include Lennard-Jones potentials, Coulomb electrostatics, and Buckingham potentials. The System constructor validates that all pairwise interactions are subtypes of `PairwiseInteraction` and issues warnings if a neighbor finder is not used with interactions that require neighbor lists.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L15-L30), [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L560-L570)

### Specific Interactions

The `specific_inter_lists` field organizes interactions between predetermined atom groups into type-parameterized structures:

| Interaction Type | Number of Atoms | Fields | Typical Use |
|------------------|-----------------|--------|-------------|
| `InteractionList1Atoms` | 1 | `is`, `inters`, `types` | Position restraints |
| `InteractionList2Atoms` | 2 | `is`, `js`, `inters`, `types` | Bonds, non-bonded exclusions |
| `InteractionList3Atoms` | 3 | `is`, `js`, `ks`, `inters`, `types` | Bond angles |
| `InteractionList4Atoms` | 4 | `is`, `js`, `ks`, `ls`, `inters`, `types` | Torsions, improper angles |

These structures store integer atom indices (`is`, `js`, `ks`, `ls`) and corresponding interaction parameters (`inters`), enabling vectorized computation of specific interaction energies and forces. The `types` field stores string identifiers for interaction type identification in differentiable simulations and parameter injection.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L40-L100)

### General Interactions

The `general_inters` field contains interactions that involve all atoms collectively, such as implicit solvent models (GBSA). These interactions implement the AtomsCalculators.jl interface and can compute energy contributions based on the full system state rather than individual atom pairs or clusters.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L415-L420)

## Topology and Molecular Connectivity

The `topology` field stores a `MolecularTopology` object containing three critical data structures:

1. **`atom_molecule_inds`**: A `Vector{Int32}` mapping each atom to its molecule index
2. **`molecule_atom_counts`**: A `Vector{Int32}` storing the number of atoms in each molecule
3. **`bonded_atoms`**: A `Vector{Tuple{Int32, Int32}}` listing bonded atom pairs

This topology information enables molecular analysis, molecule-based calculations, and constraint algorithms like SHAKE that require knowledge of molecular connectivity. The MolecularTopology constructor can be initialized from bond lists using graph connectivity algorithms to automatically identify molecules and their compositions.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L350-L380)

> [!TIP]
> Topology information is optional but highly recommended for simulations with constraints or when performing molecule-level analysis. The System constructor accepts `nothing` as a default value, allowing simulations to proceed without explicit topology when not needed.

## Neighbor Finding Infrastructure

The `neighbor_finder` field stores an object that implements neighbor list algorithms to accelerate pairwise interaction calculations. Molly.jl supports multiple neighbor finding strategies through polymorphic types:

- **`NoNeighborFinder`**: Direct N² pair evaluation, suitable for small systems or testing
- **CellListNeighborFinder`**: Cell list decomposition for medium-sized systems
- **TreeNeighborFinder`**: Tree-based spatial partitioning (when available)

The System constructor validates that interactions using neighbors are paired with an appropriate neighbor finder, preventing silent performance degradations from missing neighbor list updates. The neighbor list itself is stored in a separate `NeighborList` mutable struct containing the number of neighbors and the actual neighbor pairs.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L400-L430)

## Unit System and Physical Constants

Molly.jl integrates with Unitful.jl to maintain dimensional consistency throughout simulations. The System stores unit conversion parameters:

- **`force_units`**: Units for force calculations (default: `u"kJ * mol^-1 * nm^-1"`)
- **`energy_units`**: Units for energy calculations (default: `u"kJ * mol^-1"`)
- **`k`**: Boltzmann constant automatically converted based on energy units

The units can be disabled by setting these fields to `NoUnits`, which is useful for comparison with other simulation packages that use unitless internal representations. The System constructor provides a `default_k(energy_units)` function that selects the appropriate Boltzmann constant value based on the energy unit system.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L425-L440)

## Degrees of Freedom Calculation

The `df` field stores the number of degrees of freedom in the system, which is computed during System construction:

```julia
df = n_dof(D, length(atoms), boundary)
if length(constraints) > 0
    for ca in constraints
        for cluster_type in cluster_keys(ca)
            clusters = getproperty(ca, cluster_type)
            df -= n_dof_lost(D, clusters)
        end
    end
end
```

This calculation accounts for dimensionality, boundary conditions (periodic vs. infinite), and constraint algorithms that fix degrees of freedom. The accurate degree of freedom count is essential for thermostat coupling, equipartition theorem applications, and temperature calculation.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L570-L590)

## Logger System

The `loggers` field contains a tuple or named tuple of logger objects that record system properties during simulation. Molly.jl provides a suite of built-in loggers for common observables:

| Logger | Observable | Use Case |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| `TemperatureLogger` | System temperature | Thermostat verification |
| `CoordinatesLogger` | Atom coordinates | Trajectory output |
| `VelocitiesLogger` | Atom velocities | Kinetic analysis |
| `TotalEnergyLogger` | Total system energy | Conservation verification |
| `KineticEnergyLogger` | Kinetic energy | Temperature analysis |
| `PotentialEnergyLogger` | Potential energy | Force field verification |
| `PressureLogger` | System pressure | Barostat verification |

Loggers implement a `log_property!` function that records data at specified intervals during simulation steps. The `GeneralObservableLogger` provides a flexible interface for custom observables that require specialized calculation routines.

Sources: [src/loggers.jl](src/loggers.jl#L1-L50)

## Mass Storage and Computation

The System precomputes and stores mass-related data for performance:

- **`masses`**: Array of individual atom masses extracted via `mass.(atoms)`
- **`total_mass`**: Sum of all atom masses for center-of-mass calculations

This storage avoids repeated mass extraction during force calculation, kinetic energy computation, and velocity rescaling operations. The `mass` function is generic, allowing custom atom types to define alternative mass retrieval strategies.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L225-L240), [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L590-L600)

## Type Parameter System

The System struct is heavily parameterized to enable compile-time optimization:

```julia
mutable struct System{D, AT, T, A, C, B, V, AD, TO, PI, SI, GI, CN, NF,
                      L, F, E, K, M, TM, DA} <: AtomsBase.AbstractSystem{D}
```

| Parameter | Meaning | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `D` | Number of dimensions | `3` |
| `AT` | Array type | `Vector`, `CuArray` |
| `T` | Float type | `Float64`, `Float32` |
| `A` | Atoms type | `Vector{Atom}` |
| `C` | Coordinate type | `Vector{SVector{3, Float64}}` |
| `B` | Boundary type | `CubicBoundary` |
| `V` | Velocity type | `Vector{SVector{3, Float64}}` |
| `AD` | Atom data type | `Vector{AtomData}` |
| `TO` | Topology type | `MolecularTopology` |
| `PI` | Pairwise inters type | `Tuple{LennardJones}` |
| `SI` | Specific inters type | `NamedTuple` |
| `GI` | General inters type | `Tuple` |
| `CN` | Constraints type | `Tuple` |
| `NF` | Neighbor finder type | `CellListNeighborFinder` |
| `L` | Loggers type | `NamedTuple` |
| `F` | Force units type | `Unitful.Quantity` |
| `E` | Energy units type | `Unitful.Quantity` |
| `K` | Boltzmann constant type | `Unitful.Quantity` |
| `M` | Masses type | `Vector` |
| `TM` | Total mass type | `Unitful.Quantity` |
| `DA` | Arbitrary data type | `Any` |

This parameterization enables specialized code generation for CPU vs. GPU execution, single vs. double precision, and various boundary condition configurations without runtime dispatch overhead.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L445-L465)

## System Construction Patterns

The System struct provides multiple construction patterns for different use cases:

### Direct Construction

For fine-grained control over system properties, use the keyword argument constructor:

```julia
sys = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=CubicBoundary(2.0),
    pairwise_inters=(lennard_jones, coulomb),
    specific_inter_lists=(bonds, angles),
    neighbor_finder=CellListNeighborFinder(dist_cutoff=1.2)
)
```

This pattern is useful when building systems from scratch or modifying existing systems.

### System Modification

The convenience constructor modifies an existing System by keyword arguments:

```julia
new_sys = System(sys; coords=new_coords, velocities=new_velocities)
```

This pattern is essential for free energy perturbations where atomic parameters change while preserving other system properties.

### Crystal Construction

For crystalline systems, construct directly from SimpleCrystals.jl Crystal objects:

```julia
sys = System(crystal; pairwise_inters=(lennard_jones,))
```

The constructor automatically extracts atoms, coordinates, and determines appropriate boundary types from the crystal structure.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L660-L740), [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L740-L800)

## Validation and Error Checking

The System constructor performs comprehensive validation to detect configuration errors before simulation begins:

- Array length consistency: atoms, coords, velocities, and atoms_data must have matching lengths
- GPU array consistency: if atoms are on GPU, coords and velocities must also be GPU arrays
- Interaction type validation: pairwise_inters must be PairwiseInteraction subtypes
- Neighbor finder consistency: interactions using neighbors require a neighbor finder
- Units consistency: force and energy units must be compatible throughout the system

These validations prevent subtle bugs that would otherwise manifest only during runtime simulation.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L500-L570)

## Next Steps

Now that you understand the System object and data structures, the natural progression is to learn about coordinate management and atomic details. Continue to [Atoms and Coordinates Management](7-atoms-and-coordinates-management) to understand how coordinates are stored, accessed, and transformed during simulation. Following that, explore [Boundary Conditions and Periodic Systems](8-boundary-conditions-and-periodic-systems) to understand how different boundary types affect coordinate wrapping and distance calculations.

For practical implementation details, refer to [Lennard-Jones Fluid Simulation](4-lennard-jones-fluid-simulation) for examples of building simple systems, or [Protein Simulation Setup](5-protein-simulation-setup) for complex biological systems with multiple interaction types.

# Atoms and Coordinates Management



This page explores how Molly.jl represents and manipulates atomic data and coordinate systems—the foundational structures for molecular dynamics simulations. Understanding these core data structures is essential for effective simulation design and analysis, whether you're building simple gas phase systems or complex biomolecular assemblies.

## Atom Representation Architecture

The atomic representation in Molly.jl separates computational efficiency from descriptive information through a dual-structure design. This architecture enables high-performance GPU computation while maintaining rich metadata for analysis and visualization.

The `Atom` struct serves as the primary computational entity, storing essential physical properties required for force calculations and integration. It is designed as a bits type to enable GPU acceleration, containing only numeric fields needed during simulation steps.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L229-L257), [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L250-L257)

```julia
@kwdef struct Atom{T, M, C, S, E}
    index::Int = 1
    atom_type::T = 1
    mass::M = 1.0u"g/mol"
    charge::C = 0.0
    σ::S = 0.0u"nm"
    ϵ::E = 0.0u"kJ * mol^-1"
end
```

The `AtomData` struct complements this by storing descriptive metadata that doesn't participate in force calculations. This separation allows the `Atom` type to remain GPU-compatible while preserving detailed molecular information for analysis.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L341-L358)

```julia
@kwdef struct AtomData
    atom_type::String = "?"
    atom_name::String = "?"
    res_number::Int = 1
    res_name::String = "???"
    chain_id::String = "A"
    element::String = "?"
    hetero_atom::Bool = false
end
```

> [!TIP]
> The dual-structure design is critical for GPU performance: always store `Atom` instances in GPU arrays, while keeping `AtomData` on CPU for analysis. This pattern ensures force calculations remain on-device without transferring unnecessary metadata.

## Atom Field Reference

| Field | Type | Purpose | Units | Default |
|-------|------|---------|-------|---------|
| `index` | `Int` | Atom position in the system vector | N/A | 1 |
| `atom_type` | `T` | Type identifier for force field lookup | N/A | 1 |
| `mass` | `M` | Atomic mass for kinetic energy and integration | g/mol | 1.0u"g/mol" |
| `charge` | `C` | Partial charge for electrostatics | e (dimensionless) | 0.0 |
| `σ` | `S` | Lennard-Jones size parameter | nm | 0.0u"nm" |
| `ϵ` | `E` | Lennard-Jones well depth | kJ/mol | 0.0u"kJ * mol^-1" |

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L239-L248)

## AtomData Field Reference

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `atom_type` | `String` | Force field atom type identifier |
| `atom_name` | `String` | PDB-format atom name |
| `res_number` | `Int` | Residue sequence number |
| `res_name` | `String` | Three-letter residue name |
| `chain_id` | `String` | Chain identifier in macromolecules |
| `element` | `String` | Chemical element symbol |
| `hetero_atom` | `Bool` | Non-standard atom flag |

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L342-L357)

## The System Container

The `System` struct serves as the central container for all simulation data, organizing atomic coordinates, velocities, boundary conditions, and interactions into a single coherent entity. It implements the `AtomsBase.AbstractSystem` interface for interoperability with Julia's broader ecosystem.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L469-L538)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[System] --> B[atoms<br/>Vector{Atom}]
    A --> C[coords<br/>Vector{SVector}]
    A --> D[boundary<br/>AbstractBoundary]
    A --> E[velocities<br/>Vector{SVector}]
    A --> F[atoms_data<br/>Vector{AtomData}]
    A --> G[topology<br/>MolecularTopology]
    A --> H[interactions<br/>pairwise/specific/general]
    A --> I[constraints<br/>Tuple]
    A --> J[loggers<br/>Tuple]
    A --> K[units<br/>force/energy]
    
    B --> B1[GPU-compatible<br/>bits type]
    C --> C1[SVector{3,<:Quantity}]
    D --> D1[Cubic/Rectangular/<br/>TriclinicBoundary]
    E --> E1[Optional: zero by default]
    F --> F1[CPU metadata only]
```

The System type is heavily parameterized to enable compile-time optimization, encoding dimensionality, array types, and unit specifications directly in the type signature. This design allows the compiler to generate specialized code for specific simulation configurations.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L517-L538)

## Core System Properties

| Property | Type | Requirement | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `atoms` | `A` | Required | Vector of Atom structures |
| `coords` | `C` | Required | Atomic positions (typically `SVector{3}`) |
| `boundary` | `B` | Required | Simulation boundary conditions |
| `velocities` | `V` | Optional | Atomic velocities (defaults to zero) |
| `atoms_data` | `AD` | Optional | Descriptive atom metadata |
| `topology` | `TO` | Optional | Molecular connectivity information |

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L483-L493)

## Coordinate Systems and Boundary Conditions

Molly.jl provides three boundary condition types, each optimized for different simulation scenarios. The boundary determines how coordinates are interpreted, how periodic images are applied, and how distances are calculated.

### Cubic Boundary

The `CubicBoundary` represents an orthogonal 3D box with equal side lengths. It's the most common choice for simple fluids and isotropic systems. Setting side lengths to `Inf` creates an unbounded dimension for non-periodic simulations.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L31-L69)

```julia
# Create a 5 nm cubic box
boundary = CubicBoundary(5.0u"nm")

# Create a rectangular box from individual dimensions
boundary = CubicBoundary(4.0u"nm", 5.0u"nm", 6.0u"nm")

# Create a box with infinite z-dimension (slab geometry)
boundary = CubicBoundary(5.0u"nm", 5.0u"nm", Inf)
```

### Rectangular Boundary

The `RectangularBoundary` provides a 2D simulation box, ideal for membrane systems or surface studies where one dimension is irrelevant to the physics of interest.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L84-L127)

```julia
# Create a 10x8 nm 2D box
boundary = RectangularBoundary(10.0u"nm", 8.0u"nm")
```

### Triclinic Boundary

The `TriclinicBoundary` represents the most general periodic cell with three arbitrary basis vectors. This is essential for crystalline systems and pressure-controlled simulations where box shape can change.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L128-L148)

```julia
# Define by basis vectors
v1 = SVector(3.0u"nm", 0.0u"nm", 0.0u"nm")
v2 = SVector(1.5u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 0.0u"nm")
v3 = SVector(0.5u"nm", 1.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(SVector(v1, v2, v3))

# Define by lengths and angles (in radians)
L = SVector(3.0u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")
angles = SVector(π/2, π/2, π/3)  # 90°, 90°, 60°
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(L, angles)
```

## Boundary Type Comparison

| Feature | CubicBoundary | RectangularBoundary | TriclinicBoundary |
|---------|---------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Dimensions | 3D | 2D | 3D |
| Flexibility | Orthogonal only | Orthogonal only | Arbitrary angles |
| Memory | Minimal | Minimal | Higher |
| Speed | Fastest | Fast | Moderate |
| Use Cases | Fluids, gases | Membranes, surfaces | Crystals, NPT |

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L31-L148), [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L282-L304)

## Coordinate Vector Operations

Molly.jl provides comprehensive coordinate manipulation functions that respect periodic boundary conditions. These operations are fundamental for distance calculations, neighbor finding, and integration schemes.

### Vector Calculation

The `vector` function computes the minimum image vector between two coordinates, automatically applying periodic boundary conditions to find the shortest path across periodic images.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L12-L13), [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L350-L460)

```julia
# Compute minimum image vector
vec_ij = vector(coords[i], coords[j], boundary)

# For specific dimensions with 1D boundaries
vec_ij_1d = vector_1D(coords[i], coords[j], boundary, dim)
```

### Coordinate Wrapping

The `wrap_coords` function ensures all coordinates remain within the primary simulation box, which is essential for analysis and visualization.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L14-L15)

```julia
# Wrap all coordinates into primary box
coords = wrap_coords(coords, boundary)

# Wrap single coordinate
coord_i = wrap_coord_1D(coord_i, boundary, dim)
```

> [!TIP]
> When using TriclinicBoundary with `approx_images=true` (default), minimum image calculations are approximate but fast. For exact calculations with highly skewed boxes, set `approx_images=false` at the cost of performance.

## Accessor Functions

Molly.jl provides standardized accessor functions for retrieving atom properties, following the AtomsBase interface for ecosystem compatibility.

### Mass and Charge Access

The `mass` and `charge` functions provide consistent access to these critical properties, regardless of the underlying atom type implementation.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L283-L298)

```julia
# Get atom mass
atom_mass = mass(atoms[i])

# Get atom charge  
atom_charge = charge(atoms[i])

# These also work with custom atom types
mass(custom_atom)  # Must be implemented for custom types
```

### System-Level Accessors

Convenient functions retrieve aggregated atom properties directly from the System struct.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L20-L21)

```julia
# Get all masses as a vector
masses(system)  # Returns Vector of masses

# Get all charges as a vector  
charges(system)  # Returns Vector of charges
```

## Molecular Topology

The `MolecularTopology` struct encodes connectivity information, enabling efficient determination of molecular boundaries and bonded interactions. This is essential for molecular dynamics with constraints and for computing molecular properties.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L360-L397)

```julia
# Create topology from bond lists
bond_is = [1, 2, 3]  # Atom indices
bond_js = [2, 3, 4]  # Bonded partners
topology = MolecularTopology(bond_is, bond_js, n_atoms)

# Access topology
atom_molecule_inds = topology.atom_molecule_inds  # Which molecule each atom belongs to
molecule_atom_counts = topology.molecule_atom_counts  # Size of each molecule
bonded_atoms = topology.bonded_atoms  # List of bonded pairs
```

The topology automatically computes connected components from bond lists, providing both atom-to-molecule mappings and the complete set of bonded pairs for efficient constraint application.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L375-L397)

## Creating a Complete System

Constructing a properly configured system requires coordinating atoms, coordinates, boundaries, and auxiliary data. The following example demonstrates the complete workflow.

```julia
using Molly
using Unitful

# Define boundary
boundary = CubicBoundary(10.0u"nm")

# Create atoms
atoms = [
    Atom(index=1, atom_type=1, mass=12.011u"g/mol", charge=0.0),
    Atom(index=2, atom_type=2, mass=1.008u"g/mol", charge=0.0),
    Atom(index=3, atom_type=2, mass=1.008u"g/mol", charge=0.0),
]

# Define coordinates (centered in box)
n_atoms = length(atoms)
coords = [
    SVector(5.0, 5.0, 5.0)u"nm",
    SVector(5.1, 5.0, 5.0)u"nm", 
    SVector(4.9, 5.0, 5.0)u"nm",
]

# Define topology (bonds)
bond_is = [1, 1]
bond_js = [2, 3]
topology = MolecularTopology(bond_is, bond_js, n_atoms)

# Create atom data for analysis
atoms_data = [
    AtomData(atom_type="CT", atom_name="C", res_name="MET"),
    AtomData(atom_type="H", atom_name="H1", res_name="MET"),
    AtomData(atom_type="H", atom_name="H2", res_name="MET"),
]

# Assemble system
system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=boundary,
    atoms_data=atoms_data,
    topology=topology,
    pairwise_inters=(LennardJonesInteraction(cutoff=1.0u"nm"),),
)
```

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L540-L699)

## Initialization and Randomization

Molly.jl provides utilities for generating random coordinates and velocities following physical distributions, essential for system initialization.

### Random Coordinates

The `random_coord` function generates positions uniformly within the boundary, useful for creating disordered initial configurations.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L11)

```julia
# Generate random coordinates for all atoms
coords = [random_coord(boundary) for _ in 1:n_atoms]
```

### Maxwell-Boltzmann Velocities

The `random_velocities` function generates velocities following the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at a specified temperature, initializing the system in thermal equilibrium.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L16-L19)

```julia
# Initialize velocities at 300 K
velocities = random_velocities(system, 300.0u"K")

# Modify velocities in-place
random_velocities!(system, 300.0u"K")

# Remove center-of-mass motion to prevent drift
remove_CM_motion!(system)
```

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L22)

## Coordinate Scaling and Manipulation

Various coordinate manipulation functions support system preparation and analysis, including scaling for density adjustments and center-of-mass calculations.

### Coordinate Scaling

The `scale_coords!` function uniformly scales coordinates around the box center, useful for adjusting system density during equilibration.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L25)

```julia
# Scale coordinates by factor 1.1 (increase volume)
scale_coords!(system, 1.1)

# Compress system (decrease volume)
scale_coords!(system, 0.95)
```

### Box Center

The `box_center` function computes the geometric center of the boundary, useful for positioning atoms or calculating distances from the box center.

Sources: [src/spatial.jl](src/spatial.jl#L9)

```julia
center = box_center(boundary)  # Returns SVector{3}
```

## Integration with Unitful

Molly.jl deeply integrates with Unitful.jl for dimensional analysis and unit conversion. Physical quantities can be expressed with explicit units or as dimensionless numbers for performance-critical code.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L509-L514)

```julia
# Using units (default)
system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=boundary,
    force_units=u"kJ * mol^-1 * nm^-1",
    energy_units=u"kJ * mol^-1",
)

# Using dimensionless numbers for performance
system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=ustrip.(coords),  # Remove units
    boundary=ustrip(boundary),
    force_units=NoUnits,
    energy_units=NoUnits,
)
```

> [!TIP]
> When switching between unitful and dimensionless modes, ensure all quantities (coordinates, velocities, forces) are consistently stripped of units or all maintain units. Mixing these approaches can lead to subtle numerical errors.

## Performance Considerations

The atom and coordinate management system is designed for high-performance molecular dynamics, with several key optimizations:

### GPU Compatibility

Atom types must be bits types to work on GPU arrays. The standard `Atom` struct satisfies this requirement, while `AtomData` remains on CPU to avoid unnecessary data transfer.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L596-L599)

```julia
# GPU-compatible atom array
atoms_gpu = CuArray(atoms)  # Works because Atom is bits type

# AtomsData stays on CPU
atoms_data_cpu = atoms_data  # No GPU transfer needed
```

### Coordinate Vectorization

Coordinates are stored as `SVector` objects for stack-allocated, SIMD-friendly vector operations. This enables efficient force calculations without dynamic memory allocation.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L485-L486)

```julia
# Coordinates use static vectors for performance
coords = Vector{SVector{3, typeof(1.0u"nm")}}(undef, n_atoms)

# Access is fast and allocation-free
coord_i = coords[i]
x_coord = coord_i[1]
```

## Type System for Array Operations

The System type encodes array backend information in its type parameters, enabling compile-time dispatch for CPU or GPU operations.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L17-L18)

```julia
# Detect array backend
array_type(system)  # Returns Vector, CuArray, etc.
is_on_gpu(system)   # Returns true if on GPU

# Detect floating point precision
float_type(system)  # Returns Float64, Float32, etc.
```

This type-level information allows kernels to be compiled specifically for the target hardware, eliminating runtime branching in performance-critical loops.

## Error Handling and Validation

The System constructor performs comprehensive validation to ensure consistency between atom counts, coordinates, velocities, and auxiliary data.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L586-L599)

```julia
# These checks are performed automatically:
# - atoms and coords must have same length
# - atoms and velocities must have same length  
# - atoms_data must match atoms length if non-empty
# - GPU atoms must be bits types
```

Explicit error messages guide users to resolve configuration issues before simulation begins, preventing subtle runtime errors.

# Boundary Conditions and Periodic Systems



Boundary conditions define the spatial environment in which molecular dynamics simulations occur, determining how atoms interact when they approach system boundaries. Molly.jl provides flexible support for periodic boundary conditions across multiple dimensionality and box geometries, essential for simulating bulk materials, liquids, and biomolecules while minimizing surface effects.

## Architectural Overview

Molly.jl's boundary condition system centers on three core boundary types derived from `AbstractBoundary`, each implementing the AtomsBase.jl interface for ecosystem compatibility. The architecture separates boundary representation from coordinate operations, enabling clean composition with simulation algorithms and neighbor finding strategies.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    AbstractBoundary{D,T,C} <|-- CubicBoundary
    AbstractBoundary{D,T,C} <|-- RectangularBoundary
    AbstractBoundary{D,T,C} <|-- TriclinicBoundary
    
    class AbstractBoundary{D,T,C} {
        <<abstract>>
        D: Dimension
        T: Float type
        C: Coordinate type
        +volume()
        +vector(c1, c2)
        +wrap_coords(coords)
    }
    
    class CubicBoundary {
        +side_lengths: SVector{3, C}
        +vector_1D(c1, c2, side_length)
    }
    
    class RectangularBoundary {
        +side_lengths: SVector{2, C}
        +vector_1D(c1, c2, side_length)
    }
    
    class TriclinicBoundary {
        +basis_vectors: SVector{3, SVector{3, C}}
        +α, β, γ: T
        +reciprocal_size: SVector{3}
        +approx_images: Bool
    }
    
    System --> AbstractBoundary
    NeighborFinder --> AbstractBoundary
```

## Boundary Types and Construction

### Cubic Boundary

The `CubicBoundary` defines a three-dimensional orthogonal box with independent side lengths, supporting both finite and infinite dimensions [src/spatial.jl#L30-L60](src/spatial.jl#L30-L60). This is the most commonly used boundary type for bulk simulations and is compatible with all neighbor finding algorithms.

```julia
# Equal side lengths
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm")  # 2nm × 2nm × 2nm cube

# Different side lengths
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")

# Infinite in z-direction (slab geometry)
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm", 2.0u"nm", Inf)

# From box matrix
boundary = CubicBoundary(SMatrix{3,3}([2.0 0 0; 0 3.0 0; 0 0 4.0]))
```

> [!TIP]
> Infinite dimensions are implemented using Julia's `Inf` type and prevent periodic wrapping in that direction. This is useful for interface simulations where one dimension should remain non-periodic.

### Rectangular Boundary

The `RectangularBoundary` provides a two-dimensional orthogonal box for planar simulations [src/spatial.jl#L62-L95](src/spatial.jl#L62-L95). This boundary type automatically extends to three dimensions when padded for vector operations, with the third dimension treated as infinite.

```julia
# Square boundary
boundary = RectangularBoundary(3.0u"nm")  # 3nm × 3nm

# Rectangular boundary
boundary = RectangularBoundary(3.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")

# Infinite dimension
boundary = RectangularBoundary(3.0u"nm", Inf)
```

### Triclinic Boundary

The `TriclinicBoundary` implements a general parallelepiped defined by three basis vectors [src/spatial.jl#L97-L200](src/spatial.jl#L97-L200). This boundary type is essential for crystallographic systems, anisotropic materials, and simulations requiring non-orthogonal periodic boundaries. The first basis vector must align with the x-axis, and the second must lie in the xy-plane.

```julia
# From basis vectors
v1 = SVector(2.2, 0.0, 0.0)u"nm"
v2 = SVector(1.0, 1.7, 0.0)u"nm"
v3 = SVector(1.4, 0.5, 1.0)u"nm"
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(v1, v2, v3)

# From lengths and angles (α, β, γ in radians)
lengths = SVector(2.2, 2.0, 1.8)u"nm"
angles = deg2rad.(SVector(50.0, 40.0, 60.0))
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(lengths, angles)

# With exact image finding (slower but more accurate)
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(lengths, angles; approx_images=false)
```

The `approx_images` parameter controls the minimum image convention strategy. When `true` (default), an efficient approximation is used that is exact for distances shorter than half the shortest box dimension. When `false`, all 26 periodic images are explicitly checked for the closest one [src/spatial.jl#L487-L500](src/spatial.jl#L487-L500).

| Property | CubicBoundary | RectangularBoundary | TriclinicBoundary |
|----------|---------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **Dimensions** | 3D | 2D | 3D |
| **Basis vectors** | Orthogonal | Orthogonal | General parallelepiped |
| **Infinite dimensions** | Supported | Supported | Not supported |
| **Tree neighbor finder** | Compatible | Compatible | Incompatible |
| **Construction** | Side lengths | Side lengths | Basis vectors or (lengths, angles) |

## Coordinate Operations with Periodic Boundaries

### Minimum Image Convention

The minimum image convention ensures that distances between atoms are computed to the closest periodic image, critical for force calculations in periodic systems. Molly.jl implements this through the `vector()` and `vector_1D()` functions [src/spatial.jl#L397-L485](src/spatial.jl#L397-L485).

For 1D coordinates (used internally for each axis in orthogonal boundaries):

```julia
# Displacement with periodic wrapping
v12 = vector_1D(4.0u"nm", 9.0u"nm", 10.0u"nm")  # Returns -2.0u"nm"
# The path through the boundary (9→10→0→4) is shorter than direct path
```

For multidimensional coordinates:

```julia
# 3D displacement with minimum image convention
coord1 = SVector(4.0, 1.0, 6.0)u"nm"
coord2 = SVector(6.0, 9.0, 4.0)u"nm"
boundary = CubicBoundary(SVector(10.0, 10.0, 10.0)u"nm")
dr = vector(coord1, coord2, boundary)
# Returns SVector(2.0, -2.0, -2.0)u"nm"
```

The triclinic boundary implementation uses a sequential wrapping strategy that accounts for the non-orthogonal geometry, applying transformations in the z, y, then x directions to ensure correct minimum image identification [src/spatial.jl#L465-L485](src/spatial.jl#L465-L485).

> [!TIP]
> The minimum image convention assumes the largest non-bonded interaction distance is less than half the box size. If this assumption is violated, you may encounter artifacts. In such cases, increase the box size or use a larger cutoff distance.

### Coordinate Wrapping

Coordinate wrapping ensures atoms remain within the simulation box, applied automatically during integration steps [src/spatial.jl#L540-L560](src/spatial.jl#L540-L560). This is essential for maintaining correct periodic boundary conditions over long simulations.

```julia
# Wrap individual 1D coordinate
wrapped = wrap_coord_1D(12.5u"nm", 10.0u"nm")  # Returns 2.5u"nm"

# Wrap 2D coordinates
coord = SVector(12.0, -3.0)u"nm"
boundary = RectangularBoundary(10.0u"nm", 5.0u"nm")
wrapped = wrap_coords(coord, boundary)  # Returns SVector(2.0, 2.0)u"nm"

# Wrap 3D coordinates
coord = SVector(11.0, -2.0, 6.0)u"nm"
boundary = CubicBoundary(SVector(10.0, 5.0, 4.0)u"nm")
wrapped = wrap_coords(coord, boundary)  # Returns SVector(1.0, 3.0, 2.0)u"nm"
```

Simulators automatically apply coordinate wrapping at each integration step, as seen in the VelocityVerlet implementation where coordinates are wrapped after position updates [src/simulators.jl#L93-L94](src/simulators.jl#L93-L94):

```julia
sys.coords .+= sys.velocities .* sim.dt .+ accels_t .* dt_sq_div2
sys.coords .= wrap_coords.(sys.coords, (sys.boundary,))
```

### Coordinate Unwrapping

For trajectory analysis and visualization, you may need to reconstruct continuous paths that cross periodic boundaries. The `unwrap_global()` function uses molecular topology and neighbor information to produce unwrapped coordinates [src/spatial.jl#L600-L650](src/spatial.jl#L600-L650):

```julia
# Unwrap coordinates using bond topology
unwrapped = unwrap_global(system.coords, system.boundary, system.topology)

# Include neighbor list for non-bonded continuity
neighbors = find_neighbors(system)
unwrapped = unwrap_global(system.coords, system.boundary, 
                          system.topology; neighbors=neighbors)
```

## Boundary Properties and Analysis

### Geometric Properties

Molly.jl provides functions for computing key geometric properties of boundary boxes [src/spatial.jl#L319-L405](src/spatial.jl#L319-L405):

```julia
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")

# Volume (or area for 2D boundaries)
vol = volume(boundary)  # Returns 24.0u"nm^3"

# Box center
center = box_center(boundary)  # Returns SVector(1.0, 1.5, 2.0)u"nm"

# Density (requires system with mass information)
sys = System(atoms=atoms, coords=coords, boundary=boundary)
rho = density(sys)  # Returns density in kg/m³

# Scale boundary (isotropic)
scaled = scale_boundary(boundary, 1.1)  # 10% larger in all dimensions

# Scale boundary (anisotropic)
scaled = scale_boundary(boundary, SVector(1.1, 1.2, 1.3))
```

For infinite boundaries, `volume()` returns `Inf` and `density()` returns `0`, reflecting that these quantities are undefined in non-periodic directions [src/spatial.jl#L330-L355](src/spatial.jl#L330-L355).

### Box Matrix and Cell Vectors

The `boxmatrix()` function provides a 3×3 matrix representation of the boundary vectors, useful for interfacing with external tools and analysis [src/spatial.jl#L71-L79](src/spatial.jl#L71-L79):

```julia
# Cubic boundary
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")
box_matrix = boxmatrix(boundary)
# Returns SMatrix{3,3}([2.0 0 0; 0 3.0 0; 0 0 4.0]u"nm")

# Triclinic boundary
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(lengths, angles)
box_matrix = boxmatrix(boundary)
# Returns matrix where columns are basis vectors

# AtomsBase interface
cell_vectors = AtomsBase.cell_vectors(boundary)
# Returns tuple of basis vectors
```

The invert_box_vectors function computes the reciprocal box vectors, essential for converting between Cartesian and fractional coordinates [src/spatial.jl#L293-L315](src/spatial.jl#L293-L315):

```julia
reciprocal = invert_box_vectors(boundary)
# Used internally for coordinate transformations
```

## Integration with Simulation Components

### System Integration

The `System` struct stores the boundary as a required component [src/types.jl#L444-L500](src/types.jl#L444-L500):

```julia
system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm"),
    velocities=velocities,
    # ... other parameters
)

# Access boundary
boundary = system.boundary

# Check for infinite boundaries
has_infinite = has_infinite_boundary(system)
n_infinite = n_infinite_dims(system)
```

### Neighbor Finding

All neighbor finding algorithms in Molly.jl use the boundary for distance calculations [src/neighbors.jl#L60-L110](src/neighbors.jl#L60-L110):

```julia
# Distance-based neighbor finder
finder = DistanceNeighborFinder(
    eligible=eligible_matrix,
    dist_cutoff=1.0u"nm",
    special=special_matrix,
    n_steps=10
)

# The find_neighbors function uses vector() with boundary
neighbors = find_neighbors(system, finder)
# Internally computes: vector(coord_i, coord_j, system.boundary)
```

The `TreeNeighborFinder` explicitly requires finite boundaries and does not support `TriclinicBoundary` [src/neighbors.jl#L180-L185](src/neighbors.jl#L180-L185):

```julia
# Tree neighbor finder (CPU, optimized for large systems)
finder = TreeNeighborFinder(
    eligible=eligible_matrix,
    dist_cutoff=1.0u"nm"
)
# Only works with CubicBoundary or RectangularBoundary (finite)
```

### Force Calculations

Pairwise interactions use the boundary through the `vector()` function for computing interatomic distances and directions. For example, the Lennard-Jones interaction [src/interactions/lennard_jones.jl#L60-L80](src/interactions/lennard_jones.jl#L60-L80):

```julia
# In force calculation kernels
dr = vector(coords[i], coords[j], boundary)
r = norm(dr)
f = pairwise_force(interaction, r, params)
```

This ensures that all force calculations respect periodic boundary conditions automatically, regardless of the interaction type.

## Practical Examples

### Setting Up a Periodic Liquid Simulation

```julia
using Molly

# Define cubic boundary for liquid simulation
boundary = CubicBoundary(3.0u"nm")  # 3nm cube

# Create water molecules (simplified)
n_water = 100
coords = [random_coord(boundary) for _ in 1:n_water]
velocities = random_velocities(coords, 300u"K")
atoms = [Atom(atom_type=1, mass=18.0u"g/mol", 
              charge=0.0u"e_au", σ=0.3u"nm", ϵ=0.65u"kJ * mol^-1") 
         for _ in 1:n_water]

# Define interactions with cutoff
lj = LennardJones(use_neighbors=true, 
                  cutoff=DistanceCutoff(1.0u"nm"))

# Create system
system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=boundary,
    velocities=velocities,
    pairwise_inters=(lj,),
    neighbor_finder=DistanceNeighborFinder(
        eligible=trues(n_water, n_water),
        dist_cutoff=1.2u"nm",
        n_steps=10
    )
)

# Run simulation with periodic boundary conditions
simulator = VelocityVerlet(dt=0.002u"ps", coupling=AndersenThermostat(300u"K"))
simulate!(system, simulator, 1000)
```

### Slab Geometry with Mixed Boundary Conditions

```julia
# Slab with periodic in x,y but infinite in z
boundary = CubicBoundary(5.0u"nm", 5.0u"nm", Inf)

# Verify infinite dimension
println("Has infinite boundary: ", has_infinite_boundary(system))
println("Number of infinite dimensions: ", n_infinite_dims(system))

# This is useful for interface simulations
# Atoms can move freely in z-direction without wrapping
```

### Triclinic Crystal Simulation

```julia
# Triclinic box for crystal simulation
a, b, c = 2.5u"nm", 3.0u"nm", 3.5u"nm"
α, β, γ = 70°, 80°, 90°
boundary = TriclinicBoundary(SVector(a, b, c), SVector(α, β, γ))

# Verify geometry
println("Volume: ", volume(boundary))
println("Center: ", box_center(boundary))
println("Basis vectors: ", AtomsBase.cell_vectors(boundary))

# Create crystal coordinates (simplified)
coords = [SVector(x, y, z) .* boundary.basis_vectors 
          for x in 0:0.2:1, y in 0:0.2:1, z in 0:0.2:1]

system = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=boundary,
    # ... interactions
)
```

## Best Practices and Considerations

### Box Size Selection

When selecting boundary dimensions, ensure the box is large enough to avoid artifacts from periodic images:

- The cutoff distance should be ≤ half the smallest box dimension
- For liquid simulations, use at least 3× the correlation length of the property of interest
- For crystal simulations, use integer multiples of the unit cell dimensions

```julia
# Good practice: verify cutoff constraint
cutoff = 1.0u"nm"
min_box_side = minimum(boundary.side_lengths)
@assert cutoff < min_box_side / 2 "Cutoff too large for periodic box"
```

### Temperature and Pressure Control

Boundary conditions interact with temperature and pressure coupling algorithms:

```julia
# Berendsen barostat scales the boundary
barostat = BerendsenBarostat(1u"bar", 1.0u"ps", 
                             thermostat=AndersenThermostat(300u"K"))

# The barostat automatically scales coordinates and boundary
simulator = VelocityVerlet(dt=0.002u"ps", coupling=barostat)
```

### GPU Considerations

When using GPU acceleration, ensure boundary types are compatible with your chosen neighbor finder [src/neighbors.jl#L25-L55](src/neighbors.jl#L25-L55):

```julia
using CUDA

# Transfer system to GPU
atoms_gpu = cu(atoms)
coords_gpu = cu(coords)

# GPUNeighborFinder is recommended for NVIDIA GPUs
finder = GPUNeighborFinder(
    eligible=cu(trues(n_atoms, n_atoms)),
    dist_cutoff=1.2u"nm",
    special=cu(zeros(Bool, n_atoms, n_atoms))
)

# Works with any boundary type on GPU
system_gpu = System(
    atoms=atoms_gpu,
    coords=coords_gpu,
    boundary=boundary,  # Boundary stays on CPU
    neighbor_finder=finder
)
```

### Visualization

When visualizing periodic systems, consider whether to show periodic images:

```julia
using MollyGLMakie

# Visualize with periodic images
visualize(system, boundary_lines=true)

# Visualize single box
visualize(system, show_box=true, boundary_lines=false)
```

The `bounding_box_lines()` function provides line coordinates for drawing box outlines in 3D plots [src/spatial.jl#L368-L395](src/spatial.jl#L368-L395).

## Next Steps

- **[Unitful Integration and Physical Units](9-unitful-integration-and-physical-units)** - Learn about physical units and unit handling in Molly.jl

# Unitful Integration and Physical Units



This page explains how Molly.jl integrates with Unitful.jl to provide comprehensive physical unit handling, ensuring dimensional consistency and preventing common unit conversion errors in molecular dynamics simulations. The unit system supports both molecular-scale units (nm, ps, kJ/mol) and SI units, with strict validation to catch inconsistencies early in simulation setup.

## Unit System Architecture

Molly's unit architecture centers around three core concepts: **unit consistency validation**, **molar vs. non-molar unit distinction**, and **default unit conventions**. The system automatically validates all physical quantities during System construction, ensuring that coordinates, velocities, masses, energies, and forces all use compatible units.

The System struct stores explicit unit fields for energies and forces, which propagate through all calculations. The Boltzmann constant `k` is automatically selected based on energy units (using `k * Na` for molar units, `k` for absolute units), making temperature-dependent calculations seamless across unit conventions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[System Construction] --> B{Energy Units Type}
    B -->|kJ/mol| C[Molar Mode: k × Na]
    B -->|J| D[Absolute Mode: k]
    B -->|NoUnits| E[Unitless Mode]
    C --> F[Force Units: Energy/Length]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G[Validation Check]
    G --> H{Consistency?}
    H -->|Yes| I[System Ready]
    H -->|No| J[Error: Mismatched Units]
    
    style C fill:#90EE90
    style D fill:#87CEEB
    style E fill:#FFD700
    style J fill:#FFB6C1
```

## Supported Unit Dimensions

Molly validates physical quantities against specific dimensional requirements. Each category has allowed dimension types:

| Quantity Type | Valid Dimensions | Examples |
|---------------|------------------|----------|
| **Coordinates** | Length (L) or NoDims | `1.0u"nm"`, `2.0u"Å"`, `3.0` (unitless) |
| **Velocities** | Length×Time⁻¹ or NoDims | `0.1u"nm/ps"`, `100u"m/s"`, `1.5` |
| **Masses** | Mass (M) or Mass/Mole (MN⁻¹) or NoDims | `12.0u"u"`, `18.0u"g/mol"`, `1.0` |
| **Energy** | L²MT⁻², L²MN⁻¹T⁻², or NoDims | `1.0u"kJ/mol"`, `4.18u"J"`, `10.0` |
| **Force** | LMT⁻², LMN⁻¹T⁻², or NoDims | `100u"kJ/mol/nm"`, `1.0u"N"`, `5.0` |

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L75-L120)

### Molar vs. Non-Molar Unit Consistency

The system enforces a critical consistency rule: **all energy-related quantities must use the same molar convention**. You cannot mix molar and non-molar units within a single system.

```julia
# Valid: All molar units
System(atoms, coords, boundary,
       energy_units=u"kJ * mol^-1",
       force_units=u"kJ * mol^-1 * nm^-1")

# Valid: All non-molar units
System(atoms, coords, boundary,
       energy_units=u"J",
       force_units=u"N")

# Invalid: Mixed molar/non-molar
System(atoms, coords, boundary,
       energy_units=u"kJ * mol^-1",  # Molar
       force_units=u"N")              # Non-molar → Error!
```

This validation occurs in the `check_system_units` function, which detects inconsistencies and throws descriptive error messages early in the simulation setup process.

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L25-L58)

## Default Unit Conventions

Molly establishes sensible defaults aligned with molecular simulation practice:

- **Length units**: `nm` (nanometers)
- **Energy units**: `kJ * mol^-1` (kilojoules per mole)
- **Force units**: `kJ * mol^-1 * nm^-1` (kilojoules per mole per nanometer)
- **Time units**: `ps` (picoseconds) - used internally for velocity conversions
- **Temperature units**: `K` (Kelvin)

These defaults are applied automatically when constructing a System unless explicitly overridden. The force units are derived from energy units divided by length units, ensuring dimensional consistency.

Sources: [src/types.jl](src/types.jl#L500-L550)

## Atom and Interaction Parameters

Atoms store physical parameters with units, particularly the Lennard-Jones parameters `σ` (distance parameter) and `ϵ` (energy parameter):

```julia
Atom(index=1,
     atom_type="C",
     mass=12.011u"u",           # Unified atomic mass units
     σ=0.34u"nm",               # Lennard-Jones distance
     ϵ=0.36u"kJ * mol^-1")      # Lennard-Jones energy
```

The `check_other_units` function validates that atom parameter units match the system's coordinate and energy units. This prevents mismatches such as using Ångstroms for coordinates while specifying `σ` in nanometers.

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L60-L100)

## Boltzmann Constant Handling

The Boltzmann constant `k` is automatically converted to appropriate units based on the system's energy units:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[energy_units input] --> B{Dimension check}
    B -->|L²MN⁻¹T⁻²| C[k × Na<br/>8.314 J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹]
    B -->|L²MT⁻²| D[k<br/>1.381×10⁻²³ J·K⁻¹]
    B -->|NoDims| E[Unitless conversion<br/>~0.8314 u·nm²·ps⁻²·K⁻¹]
    C --> F[Convert to system units]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G[Store in System.k]
```

The `default_k` and `convert_k_units` functions handle this conversion automatically, ensuring temperature-dependent calculations (thermostats, kinetic energy calculations) use dimensionally consistent constants. When `energy_units=NoUnits`, the Boltzmann constant is stripped of units and converted to a numerical value consistent with the unitless convention.

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L115-L150)

## Unitless Mode

Molly supports a completely unitless mode for performance-critical applications or when working with reduced units:

```julia
# Unitless system - all values are dimensionless numbers
System(atoms,
       coords,                # Pure numbers
       boundary,
       energy_units=NoUnits,  # Explicitly unitless
       force_units=NoUnits)
```

In unitless mode, all unit validation still applies: you must consistently use `NoUnits` everywhere. The system will reject mixing unitless and unitful quantities. This mode can improve performance by avoiding unit arithmetic overhead, but requires careful manual tracking of physical scales.

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L30-L45)

## Unit Stripping for Performance

For GPU computation and performance optimization, Molly provides `ustrip_vec` for efficiently stripping units from arrays:

```julia
coords_units = [SVector(1.0u"nm", 2.0u"nm", 3.0u"nm") for _ in 1:1000]
coords_stripped = ustrip_vec.(coords_units)  # Broadcasted unit removal
```

The boundary types also support unit conversion:

```julia
boundary = CubicBoundary(4.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm", 4.0u"nm")
boundary_nm = ustrip(boundary)           # Remove units entirely
boundary_angstrom = ustrip(u"Å", boundary) # Convert to Angstroms
```

These utilities allow you to work with unitful quantities during setup and analysis, then strip units for the performance-critical simulation loop.

Sources: [src/units.jl](src/units.jl#L9-L14), [test/basic.jl](test/basic.jl#L40-L50)

> [!TIP]
> **Performance Consideration**: Unitless mode eliminates unit arithmetic overhead (~5-10% performance gain) but sacrifices compile-time dimension checking. For production simulations, start with full units and profile before switching to unitless mode only if performance is critical.

## Common Unit Conversion Patterns

When integrating with external tools or data, you'll frequently convert between unit conventions:

| From | To | Conversion Pattern |
|------|-----|-------------------|
| `u"kJ/mol"` | `u"J"` | `uconvert(u"J", value) / Unitful.Na` |
| `u"nm"` | `u"Å"` | `uconvert(u"Å", value)` |
| `u"ps"` | `u"fs"` | `uconvert(u"fs", value)` |
| `u"u"` (mass) | `u"g/mol"` | `uconvert(u"g/mol", value)` |

Velocity initialization from Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution automatically handles unit conversions:

```julia
# All three produce identical velocity distributions
velocities1 = [maxwell_boltzmann(12.0u"u", 300.0u"K") for _ in 1:100]
velocities2 = [maxwell_boltzmann(12.0u"g/mol", 300.0u"K") for _ in 1:100]
velocities3 = [maxwell_boltzmann(12.0, 300.0) for _ in 1:100]  # Unitless
```

Sources: [test/basic.jl](test/basic.jl#L25-L35)

## Error Detection and Debugging

The unit system provides detailed error messages for common configuration mistakes:

```julia
# Example error scenarios:
# 1. Mixed coordinate units
# Error: "coordinates have mixed units"

# 2. Energy/force dimension mismatch  
# Error: "force_units was specified as N, but that is different from energy_units divided by length"

# 3. Inconsistent molar conventions
# Error: "System was constructed with inconsistent energy, force and mass units. 
#        All must be molar, non-molar or unitless"
```

These errors occur at System construction time, preventing runtime failures. The validation functions (`validate_coords`, `validate_velocities`, `validate_masses`, `validate_energy_units`) check consistency across all array elements and between different physical quantities.

> [!TIP]
> **Debugging Tip**: When encountering unit errors, explicitly extract the units using `unit(x)` to see what the system expects. Compare this against your input units using `dimension(x)` to identify the mismatch type.

## Integration with Simulators and Interactions

All simulators and interactions respect the system's unit conventions without additional configuration:

```julia
# Simulators automatically use system.k for temperature calculations
thermostat = VelocityRescaleThermostat(300.0u"K")  # Units work with any energy mode

# Interactions inherit units from atom parameters and boundary
LennardJones(cutoff=1.0u"nm")  # Distance in system length units
HarmonicBond(k=1000.0u"kJ/mol/nm^2", r0=0.154u"nm")  # Force constant uses system energy/length
```

The coupling and interaction layers are designed to work seamlessly with whichever unit convention the System uses, with all unit conversions handled transparently by the core unit infrastructure.

Sources: [src/interactions/lennard_jones.jl](src/interactions/lennard_jones.jl#L1-L30), [src/interactions/harmonic_bond.jl](src/interactions/harmonic_bond.jl#L1-L30), [src/coupling.jl](src/coupling.jl#L30-L60)

## Next Steps

Understanding Molly's unit system is essential for correct simulation setup. For practical application, proceed to:

- **[Pairwise Interactions: Lennard-Jones and Coulomb](10-pairwise-interactions-lennard-jones-and-coulomb)** - See how units apply in specific force calculations
- **[Integration Methods: Verlet, Velocity Verlet, and Langevin](15-integration-methods-verlet-velocity-verlet-and-langevin)** - Understand how units propagate through time integration
